findings.title: Exact articulation beyond the terminal cut
findings.claim: Writing cuts and extends matter into countable units, but no terminal cut contains the precisely articulated divine words.
findings.mechanism: The carrier chain begins with the qalam as a pared instrument, continues through m-d-d as connected extension, and ends at the named depletion endpoint that mā denies for kalimāt. The final ḥakīm predicate contacts those articulated words and keeps the image ordered rather than vague. Together these relations shift the comparison from three quantities to operations—cutting, extending, articulating, and refusing exhaustion. The HFT’s before-reading was: “Pens, ink, and words are merely three quantities being compared.” The after-reading was: “The ayah contrasts operations: writing cuts and extends matter into countable units, but no terminal cut contains the precisely articulated divine words.”
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can see why precise segmentation still does not make the writing budget exhaustive.
findings.containment: This is an attributed inscription analogy, not a claim that the words are physical marks or that a literal writing process continues forever.
